Chapter 210: 0207 The Age of Frenzy Capital

On the 28th day of the twelfth lunar month, Chen Guiliang flew back to Rongcheng, then took a car back to his hometown in the countryside.

It was mainly to visit his relatives.

Especially his paternal great-grandmother, who didn't have many years left. Every visit was one less chance to see her.

Chen Guiliang also went to the hospital for a full-body check-up, using it as an excuse to drag his uncle Feng Tao along. He was hoping to find some issue, lest stomach cancer appear out of the blue in the future.

The result of the check-up was that Feng Tao's health was excellent…

On this year's Spring Festival Gala, Baiyun and Heitu made another appearance: Your grandpa will always be your grandpa!

Chen Guiliang, accompanying his parents and grandmother, watched the TV and laughed heartily.

On the fifth day of the Lunar New Year, Chen Guiliang left his hometown to return to the city.

His grandmother boiled ten eggs for him, and his mother stuffed his bags with lots of cured meat and sausages.

His father drove him to the city on his Jialing motorcycle to catch a ride.

He couldn't be bothered to wait for the long-distance bus, and tickets were hard to buy anyway, so he hailed a taxi directly.

Leaving the countryside and arriving in the city, time seemed to suddenly speed up.

From the moment he got in the car, Chen Guiliang was constantly making calls and sending texts: the venture capital firms were coming, and four or five of them were interested in ByteDance.

The taxi driver watched Chen Guiliang in the rearview mirror the entire way.

Chen Guiliang hung up the phone and reminded the driver, "Sir, please watch the road. Don't stare at me."

"Are you Boss Chen?" the driver asked.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Happy New Year."

"You're really Boss Chen? You're crazy famous in Longdu!" the driver said, quite excited.

As he made small talk with the driver, Tao Xue sent another text, asking when Chen Guiliang would be back in Beijing.

Chen Guiliang chatted with the driver while texting Tao Xue.

At five in the afternoon, he was finally back at Peking University.

Dorm room 404 was empty. Not a single roommate had returned.

The next day, he went to ByteDance and Game Science to visit the employees who had stayed at the company during the Spring Festival. He brought red envelopes and was treating them to dinner that night.

Chang Zhongxiang, who was usually in charge of the company's finances and had been in contact with venture capitalists recently, came to Chen Guiliang's office and said, "The VC firms have gone crazy. From what I've heard, they didn't even rest during the Spring Festival. Some firms started negotiations on the second day of the New Year!"

"Is there big news from the US?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Chang Zhongxiang nodded. "Large-scale venture investment in the US started after last Christmas. Especially after New Year's Day, multiple huge investments were closed within two months. There were rumors about Facebook's Series B funding before Christmas, but there's still no specific news. I guess the funding amount is too large for just one or two firms to handle."

If things were crazy in the US, China was bound to follow!

"Keep an eye on the news, both domestic and international. We'll take our time with the talks," Chen Guiliang instructed.

It really was crazy.

Just after the Lantern Festival, news broke: SoftBank SAEF invested 5 million USD in 58.com.

Although details like equity and valuation weren't disclosed, it still set the internet industry ablaze. The general speculation was a post-money valuation of over 30 million USD.

58.com had only been founded a little over two months ago!

It was even more absurd than Chen Guiliang's funding round last year.

Following that, within just half a month, two more VC deals were closed.

ChinaBBS received 10 million USD in investment and was officially renamed Daqi.com, with a post-money valuation of about 50 million USD.

Qihoo received 20 million USD in investment, with a post-money valuation of about 100 million USD.

Chen Guiliang was currently reading the financial news. The article's title was: "'Frenzy Capital' 2006—Venture Capital or 'Frenzy Capital'?"

The original article was in a print financial magazine and was quickly republished by major portal websites.

This financial article had broken out of its circle.

The term "Frenzy Capital" attracted a large number of readers, and the content sparked heated discussions among netizens.

Even the aunties shopping at the markets in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen now knew what venture capital firms were: they were here to give away money in China.

"We have just passed what VC managers called a 'crazy' 2005. At the very start of the new calendar year, Rock Mobile announced a successful funding round of 30 million USD…"

"Subsequently, as news of huge funding rounds for ChinaBBS, Qihoo, 58.com, and others continued to break, people's ears were filled with the question of 'who will be the next Baidu'…"

"After nearly 5 years of silence, venture capital in China seems to be heading for another peak. Leading this wave of investment fever are still the IT and new media industries… How do those VC managers in suits, carrying laptops, but controlling hundreds of millions of US dollars, decide which lucky entrepreneurs to give their cash to?"

"In 2006, how many new tycoons like Ma Yun and Chen Tianqiao will be born? What kind of game are the entrepreneurs and VCs playing? Amidst this restless VC craze, we attempt to uncover the stories behind them…"

Chen Guiliang finished the article and closed the news page with a smile.

The new year had just begun, and the term "Frenzy Capital" had already set the tone for the year.

The one actually looking for venture capital for ByteDance was Zhang Suyang, the director sent by IDG.

Zhang Suyang called and said, "IDG and DJ intend to follow on this time. Sequoia, SoftBank, Carlyle, and DCM have also expressed interest in investing."

Chen Guiliang said, "I think we should determine Tudou.com's valuation first. Hasn't IDG always been interested in Tudou.com?"

"Ah, I understand what you mean," Zhang Suyang sighed.

Soon after, with Zhang Suyang acting as the go-between and bringing in GGV Capital and JAFCO Asia, they contacted and negotiated with Wang Wei of Tudou.com.

The talks went very quickly.

Because Tudou.com's equity, financials, and data were all clear at a glance, the preliminary due diligence could be done in a day or two.

The three investment firms jointly invested 8.5 million USD, giving Tudou.com a post-money valuation of 40 million USD!

It would have been impossible to get that much before the Spring Festival.

Firstly, Tudou.com's user base had grown over the Spring Festival.

Secondly, the succession of multiple VC deals had driven those investment managers into an even greater frenzy!

Zhang Suyang called again, and Chen Guiliang said, "You guys should figure out Bairain Tech's valuation first."

Without figuring that out, no substantive negotiations could take place.

But how was Bairain Tech to be valued?

Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered with these things; he had to go to class.

Today was Professor Wu's class: "Innovation Management."

Professor Wu was currently the associate dean of Peking University's Guanghua School of Management and had single-handedly founded its Department of Strategic Management. He taught both graduate and undergraduate students.

This year, Professor Wu had two research topics.

They were "Investment Strategies of Foreign VCs in China" and "The Matching Model of Technological Enterprise Innovation and Venture Capital."

Chen Guiliang was extremely popular in the Guanghua School. Students were already greeting him while he was still locking his bicycle.

"CEO Chen, good morning. Is ByteDance getting another round of funding?"

"Chen Guiliang, I saw on the news yesterday that Tudou.com seems to have secured huge funding. ByteDance's valuation is probably going to rise again, right?"

"Classmate Chen…"

Chen Guiliang chatted with them all the way to the classroom.

He chose this course partly because he genuinely wanted to learn something, and partly to earn credits easily.

On last semester's final exam, one major question provided materials and asked students to analyze Xiaonei's technological innovation and business model design.

Chen Guiliang got a perfect score on that question!

Professor Wu even left a special comment on his paper: Analysis is on point, content is comprehensive, I myself was quite enlightened.

"Chen Guiliang, over here! I saved a seat for you!" a girl waved.

"Thanks," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

The surrounding male students were, more or less, a little jealous.

Because this girl was very well-dressed, and rumor had it she was the daughter of some official.

But Chen Guiliang was unmoved, mainly due to her looks. He liked exceptionally beautiful girls. As for conventionally pretty ones, Chen Guiliang was only willing to be ordinary friends with them.

"You're here so early?" Chen Guiliang said casually.

The girl's name was Wan Nannan.

Seeing Chen Guiliang walk over, her face beamed with a smile. She removed the book she used to save the seat and said, "If you don't come early, you won't get a seat in Professor Wu's class."

The guy in the next seat said sourly, "Wan Nannan came to class early just to save a seat for you. Aren't you going to thank her?"

"Thanks," Chen Guiliang said, directly ignoring the guy.

Wan Nannan said happily, "No need to thank me. Classmates should help each other."

The guy next to them pursed his lips, wanting to make a couple more sour remarks, but he ultimately held back.

Because saying any more would just be asking for a snub.

Students at the Guanghua School were generally arrogant, and the rate of studying abroad was high. Both male and female students gave off a somewhat haughty air. Sometimes, they weren't even aware of it; it was completely subconscious.

And what about the students from the Yuanpei Program?

The jingle "Don't marry a Yuanpei guy" said it all.

So far, only Chen Guiliang had broken this curse.

Guo Feng barely counted, having been carried to success by Chen Guiliang.

"Venture capital is so crazy this year," Wan Nannan said excitedly. "From January to now, there have already been 9 investments of over 5 million US dollars."

Chen Guiliang nodded. "It is a bit crazy."

Wan Nannan suddenly changed the topic. "My dad wants me to study abroad after my undergrad. Do you think I should stay in China?"

"That's for you to decide," Chen Guiliang said, not daring to get involved.

Although he didn't know who exactly her father was, he had heard that his position was quite high.

The guy in the next seat chimed in again, "I think you should still study in the US. The study of economics in the US is much more advanced than in China. Their financial system, in particular, is far superior to China's. We should learn advanced knowledge in the US and then come back to serve our motherland."

Chen Guiliang praised, "This classmate is very conscientious."

After a few more words, Professor Wu arrived.

Professor Wu started the class by saying, "On my way to the classroom just now, I received a call from a friend. Another venture capital deal was confirmed today. That makes it the 10th VC deal of over 5 million US dollars this year."

"Wow!"

A wave of gasps went through the students.

Professor Wu smiled. "I've never seen a scene like this either. It's even crazier than back in 2000! Is classmate Chen Guiliang here?"

"Here," Chen Guiliang said, raising his hand.

All the students in the classroom turned to look at him.

Professor Wu said, "You've come at a good time. After ByteDance completes its Series B funding, would you be able to provide me with some non-sensitive, firsthand information? If you're willing, I'd like you to join my new research group."

"I might not have that much time," Chen Guiliang said.

Professor Wu joked, "The amount of time doesn't matter. You just need to provide real-world case studies."

"Alright," Chen Guiliang immediately agreed.

He definitely wouldn't fail this course.

In his third year, he could still sign up for Professor Wu's other courses and probably get high scores as well.

(End of this chapter)
